title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Neubau der Feuerwehr Hohenkirchen
description: Die AG beabsichtigt den Neubau eines Feuerwehrgebäudes in Hohenkirchen. Die Objektplanung (LP 1-4) sowie die Baugenehmigung liegt seit Mai 2026 vor. Es wird insoweit verwiesen auf die Planungsunterlagen (Anlage 01) nebst Baugenehmigung vom 19.05.2026 zzgl. Nachtragsgenehmigung vom 25.08.2026 (Anlage 02). Für die weitere Planung sowie Objektüberwachung sucht die AG mit der vorliegenden Ausschreibung einen Generalplaner. Es ist derzeit beabsichtigt, die Bauleistungen im Anschluss als Einzelgewerke auszuschreiben und zu vergeben. Die Auftraggeberin verfügt über eine Zentrale Vergabestelle (ZVS). Folgende Leistungen sind vom Auftrag umfasst: • Objektplanung (LP 5-8) gemäß §§ 33 ff. HOAI • Fachplanung TGA Elektro (LP1-8) gemäß §§ 53 ff. HOAI • Fachplanung TGA Heizung, Lüftung, Sanitär (LP1-8) gemäß §§ 53 ff. HOAI • Freianlagenplanung (LP2-8) gemäß §§ 38 ff. HOAI • SiGeKo-Leistungen Der Inhalt der einzelnen Leistungen ergibt sich aus dem Vertragsentwurf (Anlage 03) sowie den beigefügten Anlagen zur Leistungsübersicht (Anlage 04). Die vorstehenden Planungsleistungen werden stufenweise vergeben. Es erfolgt zunächst nur die Beauftragung der LP 5 (Objektplanung), der LP 1-5 (TGA-Planung) und der LP 2-5 (Freianlagenplanung) nach HOAI. Optional bleibt vorbehalten, die weiteren Leistungsphasen in einer zweiten und dritten Stufe abzurufen. Im Übrigen wird auf den Vergabeleitfaden verwiesen.

title: Germany – Construction work – GaLaBauarbeiten
description: Die Freie Waldorfschule Weilheim, gemeinnützige Genossenschaft eG, baut ein Schulgebäude für 13 Klassen, mit Verwaltung und diversen Fachräumen sowie einer Küche und Mehrzweckräumen. Es handelt sich um einen zweigeschossigen Holzbau in Massivholzbauweise auf einer Bodenplatte aus Stahlbeton. Der Neubau ist nicht unterkellert. Lage und Erschließung: Das Baugrundstück mit einer Gesamtfläche von 14.348m2 befindet sich am Narbonner Ring / Am Hardt auf dem Flurgrundstück Nr. 2297/1 in der Gemarkung Weilheim i. Obb. Gebäudekennzahlen: NRF=3.045m2, BGF=3.793m2, BRI=17.235m3. Geschossigkeit: Zwei Geschosse. Bauart: Sonderbau Schule. Gebäudeklasse: drei. Galabau: Der Leistungsumfang umfasst den Aushub von 825 m³ Boden, die Modellierung von 1.560 m³ Gelände sowie die Herstellung einer 5.380 m² großen Planie. Weiterhin werden 2.000 m² wassergebundene Decken inklusive Tragschichten sowie 1.240 m² Schotterrasen einschließlich Tragschichten angelegt. Die Erstellung von 275 m² Asphaltflächen inklusive Anschlüssen an den Bestand und 200 m² Pflasterflächen mit Granitzeiler-Einfassung gehört ebenfalls zum Leistungsumfang. Darüber hinaus werden zwei gepflasterte Rampen mit seitlichen Sichtbeton-Streifenfundamenten hergestellt sowie 26 vorgesetzte Treppen aus Beton-Doppelstufen an sämtlichen (Flucht-)Türen im Erdgeschoss gesetzt. Für die Auflage von Gitterrost-Podesten an den Eingängen werden 10 m³ Sichtbeton-Streifenfundamente erstellt. Ergänzend werden Sickermulden mit einem Volumen von 440 m³ auf einer Fläche von 1.500 m² angelegt sowie 180 m offene Dreizeiler-Rinnen hergestellt. Die Außenanlagen umfassen zudem das Pflanzen von 27 Bäumen, die Ansaat von 1.500 m² Grünflächen und den Einbau einer Beton-Zisterne mit 11.000 Litern Fassungsvermögen (ca. 30 m³). Weiterhin werden 59 bauseitig vorhandene Beton-Formsteine sowie 11 Stück 55 cm hohe L-Steine gesetzt. Zusätzlich werden 230 m Noppenbahn einschließlich Sockelstein, 135 m² Traufstreifen mit 230 m Holzbretteinfassung, 7 Solarleuchten, 15 Findlinge sowie 12 Tonnen Wasserbausteine eingebaut.

title: Ireland – Blood and fluid warming – The Provision of Fluid Warmers and All Related Consumables
description: The Contracting Authority intends to award a contract for the supply and support of Medical Grade Fluid warmers and their corresponding consumables. The Contracting Authority requires highly reliable, safety-tested fluid warming technologies. It is a requirement that the equipment must perform accurately across a range of clinical environments and must accommodate varying clinical demands ranging from routine, low-flow continuous infusions to high-volume, rapid trauma requirements. A contract of four years’ duration shall be awarded for the provision of thirty fluid warmers, any required attachments, including all support, maintenance, repair and replacement of the equipment and the supply of all sterile single use consumables. The Contracting Authority shall remunerate the successful tenderer for the provision of the required equipment through the purchase of sterile single use consumables.

title: Ireland – Medical hospital services – Multi-Party Framework Agreement for the Provision of a Non-Operative Treatment Pathway for Low Complexity Spinal Patients
description: The Contracting Authority intends to establish a framework agreement with suitably-qualified and experienced medical service providers to deliver end-to-end outpatient assessment, diagnostic and non-operative treatment pathways for a cohort of approximately 1,200 patients. These patients are currently on a neurosurgical waiting list, rather than an orthopaedic list; however, the Contracting Authority will accept tender submissions involving orthopaedic spinal surgeon review. For tenderers’ information, a low-complexity spine patient is defined as an individual with a straightforward, one or two level or localised spinal condition that requires standard surgical or medical management with minimal technical difficulty and lower physiological risk. Under the framework agreement, the successful tenderers will assume responsibility for patients from the first specialist outpatient assessment to the patient’s discharge or until a determination has been made that surgical intervention is clinically indicated. It is a mandatory condition for the operation of this framework agreement that appointed framework operators are eligible to deliver low-complexity spine procedures under the relevant National Surgical Services Framework.

title: Ireland – Vehicle conversion kits – Drive-by-Wire System for Autonomous Vehicle Research
description: 1. Future Mobility Campus Ireland - Company Profile Future Mobility Campus Ireland (FMCI) was founded to create and deliver future mobility testbed facilities supporting research, development and innovation in Autonomous Connected Electric Shared Vehicles (ACES), including Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAV) and Advanced Aerial Mobility (AAM) in Ireland. FMCI partners include leading Irish automotive and technology organisations across SMEs, MNCs, RPOs and IOTs, with support from local authorities and state agencies. FMCI operates CAV and AAM test facilities in real-world settings, enabling technology companies and researchers to test and enhance their innovations. The facilities include a road network retrofitted with interconnected sensing and telecommunications technologies, fully accessible and controlled through a dedicated control centre. FMCI supports the ecosystem of companies developing, manufacturing and testing products and services related to CAV and AAM. The system under this tender will support FMCI Research and Development activities in Autonomous Driving and Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems. 2. Purpose and Scope FMCI invites tenderers for the supply, installation, integration, commissioning, acceptance testing, training and support of a complete Drive-by-Wire (DBW) system for an autonomous vehicle research platform. FMCI has not pre-selected a specific vehicle make or model. Tenderers shall nominate a suitable right-hand-drive battery-electric vehicle platform that, in standard production configuration, is road-legal and eligible for registration and normal public-road use in Ireland, compatible with the proposed DBW solution, and reasonably available through Irish motor dealerships. The objective is to select a technically suitable and commercially viable platform, considering the DBW solution, vehicle cost and availability, and integration risk. The DBW system will support autonomous-driving research using ROS 2 and Autoware on FMCI's NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Orin platform. International suppliers are eligible to tender, subject to applicable Irish and EU import, tax, safety and procurement requirements. The vehicle is not part of the contract awarded under this RFT. Following contract award, FMCI will procure the nominated vehicle platform separately in accordance with its procurement obligations. 3. Required Tender Outcome The successful tenderer shall provide a complete solution enabling FMCI to: * source a compatible right-hand-drive battery-electric passenger vehicle in Ireland; * electronically control steering, propulsion, braking, gear selection and direction indicators using the vehicle OEM actuation systems; * retain safe and immediate manual-driver override; * provide an emergency-stop and defined fail-safe architecture; * perform controlled low-speed operation using a remote operator controller; * communicate with the DBW system from the NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Orin using a documented ROS 2 interface; * install, deploy and maintain the supplier-provided ROS 2 interface on AArch64/ARM64; * commission and accept the DBW installation using objective functional and software-interface tests; and * operate and maintain the system without undisclosed mandatory subscriptions, software dependencies or unsupported proprietary interfaces. FMCI will perform the final mapping between the supplier's ROS 2 DBW interface and the Autoware vehicle-control stack internally.

title: Surlingham Play Area
description: Surlingham Parish Council conducted a public consultation in April 2026 to gather views on the condition and future development of Surlingham Play Area. The findings highlight concerns around safety, accessibility, equipment suitability, and the overall quality of the play environment.

title: S119--VISN 5 DC UESC VA Project #: VA-27-00007644
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NAICS Code: 221122 Electric Power Distribution 221210 Natural Gas Distribution 221310 Water Supply and Irrigation Systems 1. Contract Information: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is conducting market research to identify qualified sources capable of providing the design, implementation, and operation of a Utility Energy Services Contract (UESC) energy management project for the VA Medical Center (VAMC) located at: Washington VAMC: 50 Irving Street, Northwest Washington, DC 20422-0001 2. Background: Title 42 U.S.C. 8256 authorizes federal agencies to participate in utility incentive programs designed to increase energy efficiency, enhance water conservation, and manage electricity demand. Agencies may accept financial incentives, goods, or services generally available to utility customers when such incentives support energy or water conservation efforts. Agencies are encouraged to negotiate with electric, water, and gas utilities to develop cost-effective demand management and conservation programs tailored to agency needs. If an agency meets the eligibility criteria applicable to other customers of a utility incentive program, the utility may not deny the agency rebates or other eligible incentives. 3. Description of the Requirement: A UESC enables agencies to complete energy savings projects without upfront capital investment or specific congressional appropriations. Under a UESC, the selected utility provider finances the project using its own funds, third party financing, or a combination and is repaid through the resulting utility cost savings. The Utility will: Conduct a comprehensive energy audit. Identify energy saving improvements. Design and construct the approved project. Develop and implement a savings assurance plan. Arrange project financing. Energy savings will be measured throughout the financing term to ensure repayment through verified savings. 4. Project Information: The contractor shall design, engineer, construct, commission, and, if necessary, arrange third party financing for VA identified Energy Conservation Measures (ECMs). The VA s preliminary ECM Wish List represents the full range of ECM categories that may be evaluated during development of the UESC and includes, but is not limited to: Chiller Plant Improvements Building Automation Systems / Energy Management Control Systems Heating, Ventilating, and Air Conditioning Systems Lighting Improvements Building Envelope Modifications Chilled Water, Hot Water, and Steam Distribution Systems Electric Motors and Drives Water and Sewer Conservation Systems Energy Utility Distribution Systems Energy Cost Reduction through Rate Adjustments Energy Related Process Improvements Commissioning / Retro Commissioning (RCx) Advanced Metering Systems Note: The specific ECMs anticipated for this project and evaluated for contractor capability are listed in Question 12 of the Sources Sought Questionnaire. These represent the ECM categories most likely to be pursued initially under this UESC, while the Section 4 list reflects the broader set of ECMs that may be reviewed, expanded, or refined during audit and project development. Additional Site-Specific Program Information: The Government anticipates running an accelerated chiller plant design effort immediately following Utility selection. This design effort will occur concurrently with the UESC Feasibility Study and is intended to address critical chilled water, and HVAC system needs. The VAMC is also evaluating potential tie-ins with the VA Facility Recapitalization Program, which focuses on correcting FCA identified deficiencies across core mechanical subsystems including primary and secondary chilled water, cooling towers, air handling equipment, and associated HVAC infrastructure. While these recapitalization activities are separate from this Sources Sought, the accelerated chiller design effort and any related recapitalization coordination may inform future UESC project development 5. Submission Requirements: The Government does not intend to rank submittals or reply to interested companies/firms. This synopsis is for Market Research purposes only and is not a request for proposal (RFP) or request for quote (RFQ). The Government will NOT reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparation of a response to this notice. Your firm's response is requested no later than 12:00PM (Noon) EDT, Monday, October 12, 2026. Send responses by email to Justin O Rourke at justin.orourke@va.gov. Responses must: Be limited to 20 pages, including the completed questionnaire. Exclude brochures, cover letters, and other extraneous materials. Be submitted electronically; hard copy and facsimile submissions will not be accepted. Personal visits or requests for the purpose of discussing this announcement will not be considered, scheduled, nor will replies be sent. If additional information is required, the Government may contact responding firms directly. Sources Sought Questionnaire 1. Is your business currently a utility provider to any of the following VAMC? Washington VAMC: 50 Irving Street, Northwest Washington, DC 20422-0001 2. (Large, Small, 8(a), HUBZone, Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, etc.) � 6. Does your company plan to use an ESCO partner for this project? If yes, indicate whether the partnership will be competed and describe the competition and selection method. 7. Does your company have a GSA Area-wide Agreement? If yes, provide the GSA Contract Number. 8. Provide up to three examples of financed energy conservation projects in which your firm acted as the prime contractor, joint venture partner, or first tier subcontractor. For each project, include: Scope of contractual responsibilities Location Client Construction cost and total financed amount Customer point of contact 9. Has your company performed a UESC in accordance with DOE/FEMP Guidelines? If yes, provide the project location and project dollar value. 10.� Would your company be willing to perform the Feasibility Study at risk? (Payment for the Feasibility Study will occur only if the project is awarded.) 11.� Does your company have experience coordinating rebates, incentives, or interconnect/transmission discussions or agreements relevant to proposed projects? 12.� Based on VA s preliminary ECM list in Section 4, identify your company s expertise and experience with the ECM categories most relevant to this project, including but not limited to the following� a. Building Automation Systems / Energy Management Control Systems b. Heating, Ventilating, and Air Conditioning including Boilers and Chillers� � c. Lighting Improvements� � d. Building Envelope Improvements� � e. Chilled Water, Hot Water, and Steam Distribution Systems f. Renewable Energy Systems� � g. Commissioning/Retro-Commissioning� � h. Advanced Metering Systems 13. Provide a summary of your company s expertise and past performance in implementing ECMs related to chilled water plant upgrades. Include examples of projects where your team has successfully delivered solutions for chilled water plant design, modernization, hydronic distribution systems, cooling towers, chiller controls, phased central plant work, commissioning, and maintaining chilled water service during construction. title: Industry Day - GPS-Enabled Monitoring Devices
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE / INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) Counterterrorism and Emergency Planning Branch (CPD) This Sources Sought Notice is issued for market research and information gathering only. This notice does not constitute a solicitation, a request for proposal, or an obligation on the part of the Federal Government. Participation is voluntary and at no cost to the Government. 1. Overview & Purpose The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP), Counterterrorism and Emergency Planning Branch (CPD), will host an Industry Day focused on GPS?enabled monitoring devices with integrated two?way phone call capability and associated monitoring and data?management services. The purpose of this event is to obtain information from industry on current technology capabilities, operational use cases, and emerging innovations applicable to correctional environments. Input gathered will support the BOP�s efforts to enhance inmate accountability, improve institutional safety, and strengthen the management of inmate movement and monitoring. 2. Industry Day Objectives Vendor participation will assist the Government in understanding: � Capabilities and limitations of GPS?enabled monitoring devices with two?way communication � Integration potential with BOP systems and operational workflows � Data?management tools, analytics, reporting, and service models � Security features, tamper detection, and data?protection mechanisms � Deployment and support considerations � Applicability to correctional use cases 3. Event Details Dates: October 13�14, 2026 Time: 8:00 AM � 3:00 PM Location: 320 First Street NW 8th Floor Conference Room (MAP Room) Washington, DC Vendor Presentations: Each vendor will be allotted up to 60 minutes for their demonstration and discussion. Individual time slots will be scheduled following registration. 4. Suggested NAICS Codes Potentially applicable NAICS codes include (subject to Government confirmation): � 334220 � Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing � 334290 � Other Communications Equipment Manufacturing � 541690 � Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services � 561621 � Security Systems Services Vendors may propose alternatives they consider more appropriate. 5. Target Vendor Audience This Industry Day is intended for: � Device manufacturers � Monitoring/data?management service providers � Software developers and systems integrators � Security technology firms � Research and development organizations supporting law enforcement/corrections 6. Demonstration Logistics and Requirements To assist with planning, vendors should note the following: � Vendors are responsible for bringing their own equipment and connectivity unless otherwise coordinated. � Notify the Government of any wireless transmission requirements. � Bring necessary cables, adapters, chargers, or display devices. � Clearly mark any proprietary content shared during demonstrations. � Allow adequate time for building security screening; a government?issued ID is required for entry. 7. Capability Statement Requirements Vendors interested in participating must submit a brief capability statement including: � Company name, address, and point?of?contact � Description of relevant technologies and capabilities � Applicable NAICS code(s) � Past performance or operational experience (if any) � Technology readiness and deployment model � Any scheduling constraints or preferred demonstration windows Format: PDF preferred; recommended page limit: 5 pages. 8. Registration Instructions Submit capability statements and requests to participate to: Stephanie Wyatt Email: swyatt@bop.gov Subject line: Industry Day Registration � GPS Monitoring Devices Registration closes when scheduling capacity is reached or by the date specified in the final posting. 9. Questions for Industry To support productive discussion, vendors should be prepared to address: � How does your technology address operational challenges specific to correctional environments? � What differentiates your product or service from others in the market? � What infrastructure is required to implement your solution? � How does your system ensure data integrity, communications reliability, and tamper detection? � What analytics, dashboards, or reporting tools are included? � What durability and maintenance requirements apply in long?term correctional use? 10. Disclaimers � Participation in this Industry Day is voluntary; costs will not be reimbursed. � This event is not part of any source selection process. � No contract award will result from this notice or the Industry Day. � The Government will not provide individualized feedback. � Proprietary information should be clearly labeled.

title: JSCG-P Food Catering Service at Cristobal Colon, Panama
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ISSUED FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION, REQUEST FOR QUOTATION (RFQ), OR REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP). The Government is conducting market research to identify qualified sources capable of providing Food Catering Services in support of Joint Security Cooperation Group - Panama (JSCG-P) operations at Base Aeronaval Cristobal, Col�n, Panama. The purpose of this notice is to identify capable sources, assess industry capability and availability, and obtain industry feedback regarding the anticipated requirement. This notice is issued solely for market research purposes and to provide industry with advance notice of a potential upcoming solicitation. A solicitation has not been issued at this time Requirement: The Joint Security Cooperation Group�Panama (JSCG-P) requires contractor-provided, individually packaged meal preparation and delivery services to support recurring training and operational requirements at Base Aeronaval Crist�bal Col�n (formerly known as Fort Sherman), Panama. The requirement supports Jungle Operations Training Course (JOTC) students through recurring four-day RSOI meal service during a 12-month base period, with anticipated attendance of 120 to 150 students per course. Reception, Staging, Onward Movement, and Integration (RSOI) meal service includes dinner on Day 1 and breakfast, lunch, and dinner on Days 2 through 4. The requirement also supports Rotational Training Unit (RTU) personnel during rotating training and operational periods under a 12-month base period. RTU meal support includes two meals per day: breakfast and dinner. Meal quantities and rotation durations may vary according to mission requirements. The Contractor shall prepare, package, transport, and deliver meals as individual to-go meals to support sanitary distribution under austere field conditions; buffet service and serving lines are not required. The Contractor shall remain flexible to accommodate changes to schedules, meal quantities, serving times, delivery locations, and personnel requirements while complying with applicable food safety, sanitation, hygiene, and inspection requirements. Pre-Award Food and Water Risk Assessment Requirement: The Contractor shall identify the food preparation facility or facilities proposed for performance of this requirement. The proposed facility shall have a completed and Government-accepted Food and Water Risk Assessment (FWRA) before contract award, at no additional cost to the Government (Note: The contracting officer will coordinate a FWRA for all vendors who respond to this sources sought and validate intent to participate in the solicitation process). If the Vendor does not have an established food preparation facility in the local vicinity of performance, the Vendor shall identify a proposed facility or provide a representative temporary facility, when directed by the Government, that mirrors the Vendor�s planned operational capability for Government FWRA assessment The Government shall conduct or coordinate the FWRA assessment and determine whether the facility and associated risks are acceptable at the appropriate level of approval before contract award. If the FWRA assessment or associated risks are not accepted by the Government, the Vendor shall not be eligible for contract award When time permits, the Government may allow the Vendor an opportunity to correct identified FWRA deficiencies or risks. The Government is not required to provide an opportunity for corrective action before making an award decision. Period of Performance: The Government anticipates a twelve-month Period of Performance beginning on or about 01 November 2026. The anticipated Period of Performance is provided for planning purposes only and is subject to change. Requested Information: Interested vendors are encouraged to provide information regarding their capability to satisfy the anticipated requirement. Company name, UEI, CAGE Code, Socio-Economic Classfications (8a, HUBZONE, WOSB, SDVOSB) NAICS codes, and points of contact. A brief description of the company�s experience and capability to perform the requirement described above. Confirmation of the ability to provide adequate food catering services at Base Aeronaval Crist�bal Col�n (formerly known as Fort Sherman), Panama. (Optional) Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) to include general pricing information for market research purposes. Estimated lead time from contract award to contractor's delivery or commencement of performance. Identification of whether food catering support can be provided from the Cristobal Colon area. Identification of any anticipated risks, challenges, or logistical considerations associated with performing this requirement. Response Instructions The Government is particularly interested in identifying vendors capable of commencing performance on or about 01 November 2026. Interested vendors shall submit responses electronically no later than 12 October 2026; 12:00PM Central Time to: MAJ Vernon Shank @ vernon.d.shank.mil@army.gov and SSG Edgardo Malave @ edgardo.malave.mil@army.mil. Responses should be limited to five (5) pages, excluding product literature or brochures. The Government will use the information received to support acquisition planning, refine the Performance Work Statement as appropriate, and determine the availability of capable sources. The Government anticipates issuing a solicitation shortly after completion of this market research. Interested vendors are encouraged to begin assessing inventory availability and mobilization capabilities in anticipation of the forthcoming solicitation. This Sources Sought Notice is for informational and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation, award a contract, or reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in responding to this notice.

title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/ SOURCES SOUGHT Space Force Mission Delta 9 (MD9) � SL-5 EC2-S Ground System Sustainment
description: DESCRIPTION: MD 9 is seeking market research information for an enterprise Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) in accordance with DFARS 212.70, Defense Commercial Solutions Opening. The goal is to enhance MD 9�s operational capabilities through innovative commercial solutions to acquire innovative commercial products, technologies, or services. Headquarters is located at Schriever Space Force Base, Colorado, and is the United States Space Force's designated orbital warfare organization. Its core purpose is to guarantee the United States, and its allies have undisputed freedom of action in space. The mission of MD9 is to prepare, present, and project assigned and attached forces for the purpose of conducting protect and defend operations while providing national decision authorities with response options to deter and, when necessary, defeat orbital threats. Additionally, MD9 supports Space Domain Awareness by conducting space-based battlespace characterization operations and conducts on-orbit experimentation and technology demonstrations for the USSF. To achieve this, MD 9 is comprised of specialized units, including space operations squadrons responsible for on-orbit engagements, while also being supported by dedicated cyber, intelligence, and sustainment squadrons that ensure the availability, reliability, security, and effectiveness of its mission systems. 29 September 2026 Updated: Added RFI Questionnaire Links The Government has added an Industry Request for Information (RFI) Questionnaire to support market research for the Mission Delta 9 (MD9) Enterprise Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). The questionnaire will be used to assess industry interest, enterprise-level capabilities, and the ability of potential industry partners to support future Areas of Interest (AOIs) that may be issued at varying security and access levels. All interested parties are encouraged to complete the RFI Questionnaire using the link below: MD9 Enterprise CSO Industry RFI Questionnaire: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/1jR0pKVE6v MD9 Initial Security RFI Questionnaire: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/Qe3RZKbZgL Respondents that have already submitted a capability statement are not required to complete the questionnaire. The information collected will assist the Government in evaluating the breadth of industries' interest and capabilities applicable to the MD9 enterprise acquisition effort. Questionnaire Closing Date: 12 October 2026, 3:00 pm MST Please continue to monitor this SAM.gov notice for additional information and future updates related to the MD9 Enterprise CSO and potential AOIs. RFI and/or Sources Sought: The Government is conducting market research to inform an enterprise acquisition strategy for the Mission Delta 9 (MD9) effort. This effort is intended to support the full MD9 enterprise and is not limited to a single Area of Interest (AOI) or specific requirement. Individual AOIs may involve varying security levels and access requirements based on their respective operational, technical, and acquisition considerations. At this time, the Government is requesting: Review and inputs on the unclassified enterprise Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) Completion of the Initial Intake RFI Questionnaire; and Submission of an unclassified Capability Statement from all interested organizations. Completion of the questionnaire is necessary to obtain sufficient market-research information and assess the number of industry partners capable of responding to various AOIs that may be issued at differing security levels. The anticipated effort includes support at multiple locations, including Kirtland Air Force Base, New Mexico This RFI/Sources Sought Information request has been reaccomplished to capture adequate information from Industry. If you have submitted a capability statement already, you are not required to resubmit. 22 Sep 2026 Overhaul of the RFI/Sources Sought Information effort. Released the Draft enterprise CSO for review. Please provide responses by 11 Oct 2026. DISCLAIMER & IMPORTANT NOTES: This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This RFI does not commit the US Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. All submissions will become Government property and will not be returned.

title: R706--Pharmacy Residency Accreditation Ohio, Indiana and Michigan VA locations
description: The Network Contracting Office (NCO-10) is seeking vendors to perform the following services, Pharmacy Accreditation Program services for VA Medical Locations in Ohio, Indiana and Michigan. This is a Sources Sought to seek capable sources and request industry feedback ONLY. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. Interested parties are asked to answer questions below AND submit capability statement that clearly and convincingly identifies their ability to fulfill the requirements. Detailed capabilities statement and answers to questions below must be submitted by email to Contract Specialist Josh Kovar at Joshua.Kovar@VA.gov in an electronic format, no later than 1330 EST 1:30 PM EST | October 12, 2026. As part of market research, this Sources Sought is to determine if there exists an adequate number of qualified interested contractors capable of providing the requirement. Industry feedback to the information below is requested to ensure the VA has not created a defacto sole source requirement. The Government may use the responses to this Sources Sought for information and planning purposes. DRAFT SCOPE: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) currently has more than 200 accredited residency programs across the country. This total includes both Postgraduate Year One (PGY-1) and PGY-2 programs. A PGY-1 pharmacy residency is a broad, foundational program that builds on the education from a PharmD degree. It is designed to develop well-rounded pharmacists capable of delivering patient-centered care across diverse settings. PGY-2 residencies are advanced specialty programs that build upon PGY-1 training and education to focus on a specific clinical area (e.g., critical care, oncology, administration, etc.). Multiple Pharmacy Services throughout the Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN 10) have PGY-1 and/or PGY-2 pharmacy residency programs. The estimated number of annual residency positions is 26 across the medical centers in Ohio, Indiana, and Michigan. We are proposing a Base + 4 (1-year) Ordering Periods contract for this requirement. Questions for Industry: Question #1: Response, are you interested in providing a quote for this requirement? Yes / No (choose one) Question #2: Response: If your firm is a small business, please provide the following: Please provide your company name, address, UEI and primary point of contact information. SBA Certifications, if any regarding the socio-economic status of your company including, SDVOSB, VOSB, WOSB, EDWOSB, HUB, 8A, Small Business, etc. Question #3: Will you provide your current scope of operations and locations of service and/or capability? Where do you currently work and what is your maximum service area? Question #4: Please describe your firm s typical approach to performing accreditation services. As part of your capability statement, you may include information on what portions of the work your firm normally performs in-house versus what portions are commonly subcontracted. This information is for market-research purposes only and will help the Government understand industry practices and self-performance capabilities. Capability Statement: Please provide your capability statement, which adequately supports this requirement. The applicable NAICS code for this requirement is NAICS 813920 Professional Organizations with a Small Business Size Standard of $23.5 Million Dollars. The Product Service Code is R420 Support Professional: Certifications and Accreditations (Other Than Educational Institutions or Info Tech C&A). Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement and answer questions above. This Sources Sought is only for the purpose of identifying potential sources as part of market research. No Request for Proposal (RFP), Quote (RFQ), or Invitation for Bid (IFB) exists. Responses to this Sources Sought are not quotes, proposals, or bids on which the VA can issue any contract. This Notice is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not itself constitute an RFP, RFQ or IFB. The Government does not intend to award a contract based only on responses to this Sources Sought. Responses to the notice will not be returned. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this Sources Sought. The VA will not pay for information received in response to this Notice. Do not submit pricing information in response to this Noti

title: Allatoona Lake Dam - Eight (8) Sluice Gate
description: This is a Sources Sought Notice for information on capability and availability of potential contractors interested in proposing on a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC) to fabricate and deliver contract to manufacture eight (8) new replacement cast steel sluice gates for the Allatoona Dam in Cartersville, Georgia. The delivery location is Allatoona Dam, Allatoona Dam Road SE, Cartersville, GA 30121. The anticipated delivery date/timeframe is Summer 2027. The Statement of Work includes the following: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Mobile District, requires a fabricate and deliver contract to manufacture eight (8) new replacement cast steel sluice gates for the Allatoona Dam in Cartersville, Georgia. The contractor will be responsible for casting, machining, testing, and delivering new gates that match the existing gate dimensions of five-foot and eight-inches wide by ten-foot and zero inches high (as-builts attached for reference only). Due to the intricate structural ribbing and variable cross-sectional thicknesses of the original design, the new gates require highly complex casting to ensure proper form, fit, and function within the dams existing embedded infrastructure. The contractor will then be required to deliver to the Government after acceptance.

description: Sources Sought Notice: This is not a request for formal proposals or quotes, it does not obligate the Government to award a contract. Requests for a solicitation will not receive a response. Responses to this Sources Sought must be in writing. The purpose of this Sources Sought announcement is for market research to make appropriate acquisition decisions and to gain knowledge of potentially qualified businesses interested in and capable of providing the required services. Documentation of technical expertise must be presented in sufficient detail for the government to determine that your company possesses the necessary functional area expertise and experience to compete for this acquisition. Responses to this notice shall include the following: (a) company name (b) address (c) point of contact (d) phone and email (e) UEI number (f) Cage Code (g) Type of small business, e.g., Services Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Veteran-Owned Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, Women Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Small Business, or Large Business; and (h) Capability statement that addresses the organization s qualifications and ability to perform as a contractor for the work described below. This Sources Sought is for Robert J. Dole VA Medical Center, 5500 E. Kellogg Avenue, Wichita, KS who have a requirement for contractor provided third party pharmacy benefit services to support a First Fill Prescription Voucher Program serving eligible Veterans. This program provides first or urgent fill prescriptions when VA pharmacies are unable or impractical to dispense medications, such as after hours emergency room visits, time sensitive medications from Community Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOCs), Home Based Primary Care (HBPC), or telehealth appointments. The NAICS Code is 527292 (Pharmacy Benefit Management and Other Third-Party Administration of Insurance and Pension Funds) with a Small Business size standard of $45.5 million. SDVOSB/VOSB vendors must be registered in the SBA VetCert database. Offerors capable of providing this service shall notify the Contract Specialist no later than (NLT) October 12, 2026, 1:00 pm CST via email at maria.owen2@va.gov All information is to be submitted via email to: maria.owen2@va.gov. Phone calls will not be accepted. Performance Work Statement First Fill Prescription Voucher Program Pharmacy Benefit Services 1. Introduction The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) has a requirement for contractor provided third party pharmacy benefit services to support a First Fill Prescription Voucher Program serving eligible Veterans. This program provides first or urgent fill prescriptions when VA pharmacies are unable or impractical to dispense medications, such as after hours emergency room visits, time sensitive medications from Community Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOCs), Home Based Primary Care (HBPC), or telehealth appointments. The purpose of this Performance Work Statement (PWS) is to define the scope, objectives, tasks, deliverables, performance standards, and reporting requirements for the contractor s provision of pharmacy benefit services under this program. 2. Scope of Work The contractor shall provide all personnel, pharmacy network locations, systems, tools, and non personal services necessary to perform first and urgent fill outpatient pharmacy services for eligible VA beneficiaries assigned to the Robert J. Dole VA Medical Center (RJDVAMC) located at 5500 E. Kellogg Dr, Wichita, KS, associated CBOCs, and HBPC programs, as well as additional facilities added during the term of this contract. The scope of work includes, at a minimum: Dispensing new prescriptions written by authorized VA providers, with no refills. Maintaining a geographically accessible pharmacy network with extended and after hours operating times. Adhering to VA provided emergency medication formulary lists and applicable federal and state laws, regulations, and VA policies. Providing required reporting, data, and documentation to support billing, quality assurance, performance measurement, and compliance. 3. Technical Requirements A. Pharmacy Services and Operations The contractor shall: Dispense prescriptions only for eligible VA beneficiaries presenting a VA issued ID card, at designated network pharmacies. Dispense only new prescriptions written by authorized VA providers (RJDVA, CBOC, HBPC), with no refills permitted under this program. Maintain operating hours that include 24 hour locations and extended evening/weekend access, at a minimum Monday through Sunday coverage, including federal holidays. Limit the maximum day supply to 10 days for most medications, and up to 14 days for antibiotics/antibacterial agents unless otherwise authorized under emergency conditions. Dispense generic medications to the extent permitted by law, using AB rated generics that meet all federal and state requirements, and selecting the least expensive product in stock that meets clinical requirements. Prescriptions must be provided in written form by authorized providers, and dispensing pharmacies must be able to accept and process written prescriptions. B. Formulary Management The contractor shall: Adhere strictly to the VA Emergency Medication Formulary List, dispensing only legend drugs on the approved list unless prior authorization is obtained from the VA Chief of Pharmacy or designee. Provide real time messaging and hard edits within the pharmacy systems to prevent dispensing of non formulary or prior authorization medications without VA approval. Maintain and implement a mechanism to receive formulary updates from VA and to update pharmacy systems accordingly in a timely manner. C. Records, Confidentiality, and Compliance The contractor and contract pharmacies shall: Maintain electronic records of all VA prescriptions filled, including patient signatures for each prescription received. Protect the confidentiality of all VA beneficiary information and comply with the Privacy Act of 1974, HIPAA, and all applicable federal and state privacy and security requirements. Ensure no patient information is stored on mobile devices and that access to VA information systems is restricted to personnel with appropriate background investigations and training, in accordance with VA directives. All protected health information and sensitive personal information shall be handled in accordance with VA directives, 45 CFR Part 164, and applicable VA handbooks and policies. D. Quality of Service and Counseling The contractor shall: Provide high quality service for patients and providers, with an account management team that communicates directly with the VA Contracting Officer s Representative (COR)/Facility POC to address and promptly resolve issues. Offer pharmacist counseling to ensure optimal outcomes from drug therapy, including medication name and use, dose and route, precautions, common side effects and actions, self monitoring techniques, missed dose instructions, and proper storage. 4. Delivery & Location Information Services shall be provided to VA beneficiaries associated with: Robert J. Dole VA Medical Center and designated Community Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOCs) and HBPC programs within the primary service area and additional areas added during the contract term. The contractor shall provide and maintain a list of participating pharmacies that are: Geographically accessible to RJDVA and each CBOC. Handicapped accessible. Equipped with accessible weekday, weekend, and evening hours, including drive through windows where available. The list shall include, at a minimum: facility name and address, pharmacy name and address, phone/fax, pharmacists names and license numbers with expiration dates, accessibility status, distance from VA facilities, availability of drive up windows, hours and days of operation, and normal waiting times. 5. description: Sources Sought Notice: IHS-27-SSN-PILP DataRay D4 Patient Identification Labeling Platform (PILP) INTRODUCTION Pursuant to 48 CFR Part 326, Subpart 326.603-3 and IHM 5.5-6, Indian Health Service must use the negotiation authority of the Buy Indian Act, 25 U.S.C. 47, to give preference to Indian Economic Enterprises (IEE) whenever the use of that authority is authorized and practicable. The Government is seeking to identify Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs) and/or Indian Economic Enterprises (IEE) as its first preference and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB) as its second preference capable of performing the below Indian Health Service (IHS) requirement. Any vendor responding to this notice should submit their capability statement as well as the Buy Indian Act Indian Economic Enterprise Representation Form (Attachment 1). Instructions for submission are outlined below in Response Requirement section. This is a Sources Sought Notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of qualified small ISBEE and/or SDVOSB and/or other than small IEE Firms (25 USC 47) that are capable of providing the DataRay D4 Patient Identification Labeling Platform (PILP) to support IHS and Tribal facilities. The IHS Office of Information Technology (OIT) has determined DataRay D4 PILP is the only PILP available to seamlessly replace the legacy DataRay D3 PILP architecture. Your response to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy. BACKGROUND The Indian Health Service, an agency within the Department of Health and Human Services, is responsible for providing federal health services to American Indians and Alaska Natives (AI/AN). The IHS is the principal federal health care provider and health advocate for AI/AN, and its goal is to raise their health status to the highest possible level. The IHS provides a comprehensive health service delivery system for approximately 2.6 million American Indians and Alaska Natives who belong to 573 federally recognized tribes in 37 states. IHS�s implementation of the DataRay D4 PILP under a single contract will: Modernize the planned federal baseline of legacy D3 print stations at IHS Federal hospitals and clinics currently using RPMS to the D4 platform (or �equal� solution) with dual-stack to IPv6-only migration, while maintaining compatibility with PATH EHR for future site transition and avoiding disruption to patient care and operations. Establish an enterprise Managed Services Agreement (MSA) to provide standardized support, security patching, incident response, and operational continuity for the planned federal baseline. Standardize governance for templates/configurations and establish repeatable deployment, cutover/rollback, and acceptance processes. Provide ordering channels for exception-based replacements, site buy-in expansions, new-facility stand-up, and the purchase of compatible equipment, software, services, support, kits, and consumables. Suggested North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) Code: 518210 � Data Processing, Hosting, and Related Services; size standard: $40M. Responses will not be returned. No entitlements to payment of direct or indirect costs or charges to the Government will arise as a result of contractor submission of responses, or the Government's use of such information or otherwise pay for the information provided in response. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Furthermore, responses to this notice will not be considered adequate responses to a solicitation. Confidentiality. title: Maintenance, Repair, and Preservation of YON-322
description: The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS & IMF) is conducting market research to determine industry capability and interest in performing the maintenance, repair, and preservation of YON-322. Work will be accomplished at the Contractor's facility. The Government is seeking responses from sources that can perform the following work. Geographical Area of consideration: To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. YON-322 � Length: 199 FT � Width: 54 FT � Height: 15 FT � Age: 21 YRS � Hull Type: Steel � Draft: 3 FT � Full Displacement: 2,848 L Tons � Light Load: 706 L Tons Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR) to deliver the vessel from Manchester Fuel Depot to the Contractor�s facility. Dock, wash, and clean exterior surfaces of the vessel upon docking. Replace zinc anodes on hull / Skegs. Accomplish preservation to Underwater Hull, Freeboard, Main deck, Deck house, Cargo piping and all deck fittings. Clean non-skid located Main deck, Deck house top and Cargo deck. Remove, clean and install Rubber fenders. Modify existing Piping eliminate Aft Flow Meter and insert spool. Accomplish Ultrasonic test measurement and visual inspection of the hull, Main deck, Cargo deck and Deck house top. Open, Clean, Pump and maintain clean and dry each tank/void. Inspect tanks/voids for defects. Replace Navigational lights with new LED light fixtures. Refresh Exhaust Muffler for Yanmar and Main Engine. Replace Solar Panels. Remove Antenna Support Modification. Perform Storage Locker modifications. Replace Fuel Oil Tank Piping. Replace and Calibrate Cargo Tank Level Indicator�s (TLI�s). Perform Preliminary Air test of Tanks/voids/Steel Fendering and Skegs. Accomplish a final closure inspection of each tank/void upon completion of all work installing new gaskets and fasteners. Perform Final Air Test of Tanks/voids/Steel Fendering and Skegs. Accomplish repair, replace gaskets, and adjust watertight hatches and doors. Accomplish Cargo Pump Diesel and Diesel generator maintenance and repair. Undock the vessel. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the COR. Calibration of TLI�s, shall be conducted at Contractor�s facility after fuel on load. title: SOURCES SOUGHT Data at Rest (DaR) - 400 Obsolescence Resolution
description: OBJECTIVE: The USAF E-3G AWACS provides worldwide response to situations requiring immediate and continuous on-scene command, control, and battle management using embedded real-time surveillance to support employment of U.S. and allied combat forces. The E-3G consists of the air vehicle, sensor systems, and computing and communications equipment. The current USAF E-3G operational fleet consists of 15 operational aircraft. The E-3G DAR-400 (part numbers 63-2824652-01 through -03) is a mission critical asset and is in critical need of obsolescence resolution to prevent mission impact. Since the DAR-400 contains encrypted MCS, MSS, IPEC and GS data, a failure would directly impact operations and data security. General Dynamics Mission Systems (GDMS) has notified us that the DAR-400 will not be able to support or upgrade to changing NSA requirements. SCOPE: To execute the installation and integration of the obsolescence resolution for the mission-critical E-3G DAR-400 to prevent mission impact. The provided Government-owned KG-204 based solution is compliant with current DoD and NSA mandates to replace the legacy DAR-400 equipment. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION DETAILS: AFLCMC/WIW is requesting information from industry as part of market research to determine interest level and size of qualified vendors. title: TTS for DTB Pilot - Request for Information
description: **09/28/2026: Amendment: Attachments Added, see below. This is a Request for Information (RFI) to obtain capability statements and potential feedback for an upcoming Library of Congress (LOC) requirement. Specifically, the Library of Congress (Library) requires the contractor to design software to automate the construction of digital talking books compliant with DAISY ANSI/NISO Z39.86-2002 and NLS specifications 1202, 1203, 1205, 1206 as applicable and Proper XML structure and validation for digital talking books. The software shall be capable of generating digital talking books from commercial audiobooks with pre-existing audio files, as well as from electronic text source materials that do not include pre-existing audio. The software shall automate the synthesis of speech from provided announcement scripts and/or the electronic text source materials. Automatically generate and manage XML control/navigation files and Metadata and structural elements. Support synthetic speech generation for announcements and full-length digital talking books. Handle large-scale batch processing. Shall require demonstrations or samples. The contractor shall demonstrate that the software integrates with NLS AWS systems. Supports standard file formats (audio, XML, text, metadata). Allows export/import without proprietary lock-in. Requires interface controls. The contractor shall demonstrate knowledge and experience with Amazon Web Services (AWS) sufficient to support the requirements of this contract. The Library�s existing Digital Talking Book (DTB) production environment is a high-volume, semi-automated pipeline designed to transform source text into accessible, navigation-rich audio assets. The current DTB architecture utilizes a standardized ingestion-to-distribution framework that relies on adherence to established specifications, metadata schemas, and structural navigation hierarchies. In order to obtain this information, the Library is seeking capabilities statements, rough orders of magnitude estimates, input on the Statement of Work, or any other information your business would care to provide in order to help the Library understand the possible solutions available on the commercial marketplace. All information received shall be reviewed to help the Library inform its possible future acquisition decisions relating to this requirement. Participation in this RFI is voluntary only and is no guarantee of future business. The Library is not seeking to obtain official proposals at this time as a result of this notice. The Library is seeking outside information from potential offerors as a way to perform supplemental market research. No contract shall be awarded as a result of this RFI. This notice solely constitutes market research. Under NO circumstances shall any expenses be repaid as a result of contractor engagement with RFI this notice. Offerors are encouraged to ask questions or provide feedback so that the LOC may enhance its understanding to reflect a more accurate business environment. Attached is a draft Statement of Work. Offerors are encouraged to provide feedback on this document as well, and all comments/questions/suggestions shall be considered (this is not a guarantee that they will be answered to reflected in the final solicitation). Finally, rough orders of magnitude in terms of pricing is also being asked for. Please note, these would be estimates only and serve only the purposes of market research. These are NOT official quotes, but are considered to be high level rough ballpark estimates of other marketplace solutions. Please send any questions/feedback and/or capability statements to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist listed on this notice. title: Manufacturing of Explosive Shape Charges for F-16 Spin Chute Recovery System
description: SOURCES SOUGHT / CAPABILITIES REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (CRFI) Name/Subject: Manufacturing of Explosive Shape Charges for F-16 Spin Chute Recovery System Notice ID / Unique Identifier: FA8615-27-RFI-SCRS Contract Opportunity Type/Notice Type: Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI) NAICS Code: 325920 � Explosives Manufacturing (Small Business Size Standard: 750 employees) Product Service Code (PSC): 1377 � Cartridge and Propellant Actuated Devices and Rescue Equipment Components Place of Performance: Contractor Manufacturing Facilities and/or Government Flight Test Facilities Response Date: 30 days from publication Points of Contact (POC): Contracting Officer: ?Mellisa Flanagan,?mellisa.flanagan@us.af.mil Contract Specialist: Omar Inman, omar.inman@us.af.mil 1.0 INTRODUCTION & PURPOSE This is a Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought notice issued by the Department of War, Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Fighters and Advanced Aircraft Directorate (WA), F-16 Program Office (DEPT OF WAR/ DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE/ AFMC/ AFLCMC/ WAM (F-16 Division). This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this CRFI is to conduct market research in accordance with RFO Part 10 to identify potential sources (including Small Businesses, SDB, 8(a), HUBZone, VOSB, SDVOSB, and WOSB) with the technical capabilities, licensing, safety certifications, and manufacturing maturity to produce, test, and deliver small explosive shape charges used in the F-16 Spin Chute Recovery System. The information gathered from this notice will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy, specifically whether a 100% Small Business Set-Aside (SBSA) or full and open competition is appropriate. The Government is contemplating a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract structure with an estimated 24-month period of performance. 2.0 BACKGROUND / REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION 2.1 Program Overview The F-16 Program Office requires explosive shape charges to support critical aeromechanical flight test missions. To execute high Angle of Attack (AoA) flight tests safely, the test aircraft must be equipped with a functional Spin Chute Recovery System (SCRS). A critical component of this emergency safety system is a specialized explosive shape charge used to initiate deployment of the spin recovery chute. The Government's current inventory of these devices is insufficient to support the upcoming flight test schedule. The Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of this component is no longer manufacturing it. Therefore, the Government is seeking qualified sources to produce these components. The Government may provide a Technical Data Package (TDP) for a build-to-print effort, and/or will consider proposals for an existing, qualified component that meets the form, fit, and function (FFF) requirements of the original part. 2.2 Technical Reference of the Component The component to be manufactured is a high-precision, cartridge-actuated explosive device. The requirement is for an FFF equivalent to, or a build-to-print production of the original?Shaped Charge Assembly, P/N 52238-1. Key reference parameters include: Physical Dimensions:?Approximate outside diameter of 7.0 inches, inside diameter of 5.0 inches, and 1.0 inch in height. Energetics Formulation:?Net Explosive Weight (NEW) of approximately 5.5 grams per assembly, utilizing a lead-sheathed PBXN-5 linear shaped charge and dual detonators containing RDX and Lead Azide. Electrical Interface:?Fired via an integrated 4-pin electrical connector with a bridgewire resistance of 0.80 to 1.50 ohms. Firing Characteristics:?No-fire threshold of 1.0 amp / 1.0 watt and an all-fire threshold of 3.5 amps (minimum). D.O.T. Classification:?Equivalent to Fuzes, Detonating, Class 1.4B, UN0257. 2.3 Access to Technical Data Package (TDP) & Drawings Due to the military utility and export-control restrictions (ITAR), the full TDP and associated drawings (e.g., Lockheed 16FTL076-1, ATP 11932(02)ATP) will NOT be posted publicly. To request access, interested and qualified vendors must contact the POCs listed above and possess an approved and active?DD Form 2345 (Military Critical Technical Data Agreement). 3.0 REQUESTED INFORMATION (CAPABILITY STATEMENT) Interested parties are requested to submit a Capability Statement addressing the following areas. Responses should be concise and directly address the specified requirements. 3.1 Company Information Basic Data: Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, and Unique Entity ID (UEI). Business Size & Socioeconomic Status: Indication of business size and status under NAICS 325920 (e.g., HubZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, SDB, etc.). Security & Facility Clearances: Current Facility Clearance Level (FCL) and capabilities to safeguard Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and military-grade technical data. Point of Contact: Full Name, Position/Role, Phone Number, and Email Address. 3.2 Technical & Manufacturing Capabilities Respondents must explicitly address their approach, licensing, and technical capability in the following areas: Energetics & Explosives Manufacturing Experience: Describe your experience in compounding, loading, and assembling military-grade Cartridge Actuated Devices / Propellant Actuated Devices (CAD/PAD) or lead-sheathed PBXN-5 linear shaped charges. Handling of Sensitive Energetics (Lead Azide and RDX): Confirm that your facilities are licensed, zoned, and equipped to safely store, handle, and process sensitive energetic materials including Lead Azide and RDX in accordance with DoD 4145.26-M (DoD Contractors' Safety Manual for Ammunition and Explosives). Build-to-Print Execution from Third-Party TDPs: Describe your experience in utilizing technical drawing packages, assembly schematics, and chemical specifications provided by an external OEM under licensing or government-furnished data provisions. Describe your experience with build-to-print manufacturing from a Government-provided TDP. Additionally, state if you have an existing FFF-equivalent product that could meet this requirement. Testing Capability:?Describe your capability to perform required testing, including Radiographic (X-ray) Examination (per ASTM E 1742), precision electrical verification, and Lot Acceptance Testing (LAT). Supply Chain Security & Energetic Sourcing: Detail your processes for raw material sourcing (particularly lead sheath tubing and PBXN-5 ingredients), counterfeit parts mitigation, and supply chain risk management (SCRM). Export Control and ITAR Compliance: Confirm your organization's registration with the Directorate of Defense Trade Controls (DDTC) and experience handling technical data subject to ITAR. 3.3 Past Performance Provide up to three (3) examples of recent and relevant past performance (within the last 10 years) where your company manufactured, tested, and delivered pyrotechnics, CAD/PAD devices, or explosive components for Department of War (DoW) aviation or aerospace platforms. 4.0 SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Page Limit: Responses shall not exceed ten (10) single-sided pages (including cover page). Format: Utilize Attachment 1 � Response Submittal Template. Submissions must be in PDF format (converted from MS Word), 12-point Times New Roman, Arial, or similar font with 1-inch margins. Deadline: Responses are due no later than 17:00 Eastern Time (ET) on InsertDate?30DaysFromPublicationInsertDate?30DaysFromPublication. Submission POC: Submit all response packages via email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist listed in the header section of this notice. Classified Information: DO NOT submit classified information. All submissions must be unclassified. 5.0 DATA RIGHTS & PROPRIETARY INFORMATION If the respondent�s submission contains proprietary, confidential, or sensitive commercial information, it must be clearly marked on a page-by-page basis. The Government intends to use this information to assess market capabilities and will protect pr

title: Z1DA--658-19-103 RENOVATE SURGICAL SUITE PHASE II
description: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE 658-19-103 Renovate Surgical Suite Phase II Salem VA Medical Center (Salem, Virginia) The Department of Veterans Affairs, Salem VA Medical Center in Salem, Virginia, has a requirement for a contractor to provide construction services to complete Project 658-19-103 Renovate Surgical Suite Phase II in accordance with the solicitation and any resulting contract. DESCRIPTION: Project 658-19-103 Renovate Surgical Suite Phase II: This construction services project includes general construction, structural, architectural, fire suppression, plumbing, mechanical, electrical, and fire alarm systems trades to perform work in Building 143 at the Salem VA Medical Center. The purpose of the project is to expand and renovate an existing surgical suite to comply with the current VA design guidelines and provide innovative functional spaces. This requirement corrects several outstanding deficiencies discovered during the facilities condition assessment (FCA) as a result of obsolete equipment and infrastructure for surgical services per the VA Design Manual and other dictating medical codes. The project will be broken down into four phases with each phase being completed and activated prior to the next phase beginning. The first phase will consist of creating three new operating rooms in a currently vacant area of the hospital, resulting in no impact to operating room functions. The second phase will include complete renovation of the existing operating rooms, and patients will be re-routed to the new operating rooms constructed during the first phase. Phase three will include the nursing station pre-op area. This is not expected to impact patient care as alternative areas nearby will be used for post-op. The final phase includes what is currently the post-op recovery and surgical area. The place of performance is the Salem VA Medical Center at 1970 Roanoke Blvd. Salem VA 24153. The period of performance for this project is 840 calendar days from the issuance of Notice to Proceed (NTP). MAGNITUDE OF CONSTRUCTION: Between $20,000,000 and $50,000,000. The NAICS code for this action is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (SBA Size Standard: $45.0m annual revenue). The Product Service Code is Z2DA, Repair or Alteration of Hospitals and Infirmaries. UNRESTRICTED SOLICITATION: The solicitation being issued will be Unrestricted without any set-aside. Only one award will be made. It is anticipated that the solicitation will be made available on or around Monday, October 12, 2026. The solicitation and any amendments will be posted on this website, www.sam.gov, Contract Opportunities. The solicitation will include instructions to offerors/bidders. This notice is for informational purposes only. The Government is not obligated to issue a solicitation as a result of this notice. No other information is available until issuance of the solicitation. All interested parties should register on this website. It is the offeror/bidders responsibility to check the web site periodically for any amendments/notices to the solicitation. Prospective contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database in order to obtain access in SAM.gov Contract Opportunities. Offerors/bidders must have an active SAM.gov registration at time of offer/bid submission and throughout the evaluation and award phase. Contractors please note: Representations and Certifications can be maintained, online, in the System for Award Management (SAM), at https://www.sam.gov/portal/SAM/#1.

description: Udbudsprocessen omfatter en kontrakt til Ordregivers anskaffelse af transport og behandling af A2-træ til genanvendelse fra Vejle Kommunes genbrugspladser. Tilbudsgiver skal forestå: * afhentning, transport, behandling og genanvendelse af det indsamlede A2-træ fra genbrugspladsen RessourceCenter Vejle, * modtagelse og behandling af det indsamlede A2-træ fra Ordregivers tre genbrugspladser i Børkop, Egtved og Give samt * stille nødvendige containere til rådighed på RessourceCenter Vejle i hele kontraktperioden. Tilbudsgiver skal sikre, at størst mulig andel af træet genanvendes, og at restprodukter håndteres i overensstemmelse med gældende lovgivning, herunder affaldsbekendtgørelsen. I 2025 var mængden for træ til genanvendelse (A2-træ) på 6.462 tons og antallet af afhentninger/træk for et læs á to (2) fyldte containere på 716 fra Ordregivers fire (4) genbrugspladser. Mængden og antal afhentninger/træk af træ til genanvendelse (A2-træ) forventes at variere hen over året samt mellem de enkelte år i kontraktperioden. Det forventes, at de fremtidige mængder og antal afhentninger/træk vil ligge på omtrent samme niveau. Den forventede volumen i tilbudslisten er alene vejledende og ikke bindende for Ordregiver, da de baserer sig på historiske tal. Der henvises i øvrigt til udbudsmaterialet for en nærmere beskrivelse af den udbudte opgave.

description: Elisabeth-Kallenberg-Platz 6, 71706 Markgröningen, Markgröningen, AHW-Schule, Gebäude C2 - Dachsanierung, Ingenieurleistungen nach Teil 4 Abs. 2 HOAI, Technische Ausrüstung _HLS, Beabsichtigt ist die Beauftragung von Fachplanungsleistungen für die Technische Ausrüstung von Bestandsgebäuden nach Teil 4, Abschnitt 2 der HOAI im Bereich HLS für die Dachsanierung der August-Hermann-Werner-Schule in Markgröningen.Für die Dachsanierung ist es notwendig, das vorhandene Lüftungsgerät einschließlich der Kanäle zu demontieren, vom Dach abzutransportieren, einzulagern und später wieder auf dem Dach aufzustellen. Im Zuge der Dachsanierung ist es zudem erforderlich, die Dachdurchführungen, die teilweise zu nah an der Dachkante liegen, an die heutigen Anforderungen anzupassen. Hierzu müssen im obersten Geschoss die Leitungen (HLS) entsprechend angepasst sowie die Schächte mit Brandschutzanforderungen geöffnet und anschließend wieder verschlossen werden.

buyer: Styrelsen for Grøn Arealomlægning og Vandmiljø
title: Rammeaftale vedrørende levering af trådløse dataloggere og sensorer til registrering og opsamling af miljømålinger
description: Til kundens overvågning af det danske vandmiljø udbydes en rammeaftale vedrørende levering af trådløse dataloggere med stabile vandstands-, temperatur og iltsensorer. Formålet med indkøbet er at måle vandstand, vandtemperatur og iltindhold på 35 udvalgte vandløbsstationer i Danmark som led i det Nationale Overvågningsprogram for Vandmiljø og Naur (NOVANA). NOVANA’s måleprogram er fastlagt af kundens Fagkoordineringsgrupper (FKG), som også fastlægger kravene til målingerne, deres præcision, hyppighed, m.v. Leverancen skal bestå af et samlet funktionsdygtigt sæt indeholdende datalogger, vandstandssensor og iltsensor/temperatur. De trådløse dataloggere, som er omfattet af denne aftale, skal monteres og drives af kundens lokale medarbejdere over hele landet. Målte data skal leveres direkte til den fællesoffentlige infrastruktur for miljødata under Danmarks Miljøportal (DMP), hvorfra kunden kan viderestille data til diverse fagdatabaser, som fx VanDa. Levering af målte data fra dataloggere skal ske via en trådløs dataforbindelse i dataloggerne direkte til DMP’s infrastruktur i Microsoft Azure (DMP-IoT), uden om evt. andre cloudløsninger. For at sikre stabil dataoverførsel også på fjernt og lavtliggende målestationer, hvor modtagerforholdene kan være udfordrende, skal dataloggere anvende stabile og landsdækkende telemetri-/netværksløsninger, som er tilgængelige for kunden. Det skal endvidere være muligt for en feltmedarbejder under tilsyn i felten at betjene en datalogger via en direkte opkobling eller en trådløs forbindelse, direkte mellem datalogger og feltmedarbejderes styringsdevice, dvs. uden anvendelse af telemetriløsning, således at eventuel svag netværksdækning ikke vanskeliggør kontakt med logger.

title: Netherlands – Insurance services – Collectieve ArbeidsOngeschiktheidsVerzekering (AOV)
description: Gemeente Peel en Maas wil als werkgever via een collectief contract een verzekering bieden voor alle medewerkers die bij gedeeltelijke en volledige arbeidsongeschiktheid voorziet in een uitkering waarmee de (som van de) WIA-uitkering en het arbeidsongeschiktheidspensioen ABP samen worden aangevuld tot minimaal 70% bij gedeeltelijke arbeidsongeschiktheid en 10% van het verzekerd inkomen bij volledige arbeidsongeschiktheid WGA 80-100% en 5% bij IVA 80-100%. Het inkomen dient aangevuld te worden tot aan de deelnemer geldende AOW gerechtigde leeftijd. Premiebetaling vindt plaats zolang er sprake is van een verzekerbaar belang. . Met deze aanbesteding beoogt de gemeente een overeenkomst aan te gaan met één verzekeraar, die een collectieve arbeidsongeschiktheidsverzekering in overeenstemming met onze eisen en wensen biedt. Het gaat om 427 medewerkers en een te verzekeren loonsom van ca. 20.500.000 EUR. . De overeenkomst heeft een looptijd van drie (3) jaar, gaat in op 1 januari 2027 en eindigt op 1 januari 2030. De overeenkomst kan na de initiële looptijd verlengd worden met nog een periode van drie jaar.
